justification: States predictions for content contrasts (ignition for consciously perceived versus unperceived stimuli) and for state contrasts (functional disconnection of frontal–parietal networks under general anaesthesia and in disorders of consciousness).

Conscious access is defined as global availability that can occur with or without overt behavioural report, and the preregistered protocol commits GNW to prefrontal decodability of conscious content for task-irrelevant (unreported) stimuli.

dimension: Consciousness measure type (objective / subjective / condition assessment / none)
justification: Predicts a non-linear, all-or-none threshold in subjective visibility ratings for masked stimuli, coupled to late event-related components.

Paradigm-specific predictions are stated: ignition for seen versus unseen stimuli in content paradigms, and loss of long-range functional connectivity under anaesthesia and in disorders of consciousness.

The protocol states a task-indexed prediction: conscious content decodable from prefrontal cortex in both task-relevant and task-irrelevant conditions, with decoding generalising between them in the 300–500 ms window.
Predictions are stated identically for faces, objects, letters and false fonts; stimulus category enters only as the content to be decoded, not as a variable that changes the prediction.

dimension: Sample / population type (healthy adults / patients / non-human / computer)
justification: Predicts that resting-state functional-connectivity variation present in awake participants vanishes under anaesthesia and in patients with disorders of consciousness, a differential prediction for patient populations.
Predictions are specified per technique in the preregistration: fMRI/iEEG decodability in prefrontal cortex and M-EEG long-range synchronisation.

dimension: Dependent measure / analysis type (incl. connectivity, complexity, PHI, cardiac tags)
justification: Predicts long-range information sharing (gamma/beta synchronisation) between prefrontal cortex and category-selective areas as the dependent measure of conscious perception.
Predicts ignition around 200–300 ms after stimulus onset and content decodability from prefrontal cortex at ~300–500 ms, with transient onset and offset responses rather than sustained activity.
Predicts conscious content decodable from inferior frontal gyrus, middle frontal gyrus and cingulate cortex, and that the putative NCC includes prefrontal cortex.
Inter-areal information sharing is predicted to be measurable as gamma/beta synchronisation between prefrontal and category-selective regions.
States level predictions (a theory-driven index of the level of consciousness, PCI, for sleep, anaesthesia and brain injury) as well as content predictions for posterior cortex.
Predicts that content-specific NCCs lie in posterior cortex independently of task relevance and report, with similar activity patterns for seen stimuli across go and no-go conditions.

dimension: Consciousness measure type (objective / subjective / condition assessment / none)
justification: Proposes an objective index of consciousness independent of the subject's ability to interact with the environment, i.e. a measure dissociable from behavioural report.
Predicts breakdown of cortical effective connectivity (failure of TMS-evoked activity to propagate) in NREM sleep, the state paradigm in which consciousness fades.
The preregistration states a task-indexed prediction: posterior content-specific activity invariant across task-relevant and task-irrelevant conditions and across go/no-go tasks.
Category-selective and lower-level visual areas are named as substrates, but no prediction depends on stimulus category, modality or duration beyond the sustained-activity claim.

dimension: Sample / population type (healthy adults / patients / non-human / computer)
justification: The postulates are stated to apply to any system of units in a state, yielding predictions for patients, non-human animals and artificial systems.
Predicts a technique-specific test: perturbation with TMS combined with high-density EEG to measure propagation of evoked activity.

dimension: Dependent measure / analysis type (incl. connectivity, complexity, PHI, cardiac tags)
justification: Predicts an integration-plus-differentiation measure (perturbational complexity) as the dependent variable indexing consciousness.
Predicts sustained, content-specific activity in posterior cortex throughout the duration of the percept, in contrast to transient onset/offset responses.
Predicts that content-specific NCCs are found primarily in the posterior hot zone and that the putative NCC maps onto posterior areas.
Predicts synchronisation between category-selective and early visual areas but specifies no frequency band; the gamma/beta specification in the protocol is GNW's.
Recurrent (feedback) processing in visual cortex is proposed as the correlate of visual awareness, a content claim; state contrasts such as sleep or anaesthesia are not addressed.
Argues that introspection and behaviour mislead us about what we are conscious of, so presence of consciousness must be inferred from neural evidence rather than report.

dimension: Consciousness measure type (objective / subjective / condition assessment / none)
justification: Proposes replacing report-based (objective or subjective) criteria with a neural criterion for consciousness.
Predicts that masking abolishes awareness by selectively interrupting reentrant processing, rather than by feedforward disruption.
Detection tasks are used, but no prediction is indexed to task type.
Texture-defined figure–ground stimuli are the paradigm case, but the prediction concerns feedback processing, not stimulus class.

dimension: Sample / population type (healthy adults / patients / non-human / computer)
justification: The feedforward/recurrent distinction is stated for the primate visual system generally; no population-specific prediction is formulated.
Predicts EEG signatures of reentrant processing in human visual cortex that masking disrupts.

dimension: Dependent measure / analysis type (incl. connectivity, complexity, PHI, cardiac tags)
justification: Predicts late feedback-related modulation of early visual responses (the ConTraSt 'Recurrent Processing' tag) as the dependent measure.
Distinguishes a fast feedforward sweep from later recurrent processing and ties awareness to the latter.
Localises the correlate to feedback from higher to lower visual areas within visual cortex rather than to frontal cortex.
No frequency-band prediction is stated.
A content-level account: conscious experiences regardless of content arise from one cortical system; state contrasts are not addressed.
Awareness reports are modelled as metacognitive inference distinct from states covarying with perceptual content, a stated prediction that report-related and content-related states dissociate.

dimension: Consciousness measure type (objective / subjective / condition assessment / none)
justification: Predicts dissociation between objective first-order performance and subjective awareness, quantified as metacognitive sensitivity (meta-d').
Support is drawn from existing dissociation paradigms, but no paradigm is singled out by a stated prediction.
Confidence-report tasks are predicted to index the higher-order state separately from first-order discrimination.
Explicitly predicts that emotional and non-emotional contents engage the same general cortical network, differing only in inputs, an invariance claim indexed to stimulus category.

dimension: Sample / population type (healthy adults / patients / non-human / computer)
justification: Predictions concern human metacognition; no differential prediction for patients or non-human animals is stated.
No technique-specific prediction.

dimension: Dependent measure / analysis type (incl. connectivity, complexity, PHI, cardiac tags)
justification: Metacognitive sensitivity from confidence ratings is the theory's dependent measure.
The higher-order state-space model accounts for 'global ignition' observations post hoc but states no timing prediction.
Predicts that a general cortical network, not subcortical circuits, is responsible for conscious experience including emotional feelings.
No frequency-band prediction.
Awareness is a model of attention, a content-level account; state contrasts are not addressed.
Awareness is operationalised by report of awareness; no prediction is stated for no-report designs.

dimension: Consciousness measure type (objective / subjective / condition assessment / none)
justification: Predicts that subjective awareness of a cue, rather than its objective attentional effect, determines endogenous attention control.
Predicts, in cueing paradigms, that without awareness of the cue exogenous attention persists while endogenous control is impaired.
Predicts a task-type dissociation: endogenous but not exogenous attention tasks are impaired when the cue is not consciously seen.
Explicitly predicts that awareness pertains to the same domains as attention, external sensory and internal information alike, an invariance claim across stimulus modality.

dimension: Sample / population type (healthy adults / patients / non-human / computer)
justification: Predictions are stated for healthy adults; no population-specific prediction.
fMRI is used but no technique-specific prediction is stated.

dimension: Dependent measure / analysis type (incl. connectivity, complexity, PHI, cardiac tags)
justification: Behavioural attention effects and BOLD are used without a theory-specific dependent measure.
No timing prediction.
Motivates and tests the prediction that cortical regions track awareness independently of attention, with bilateral temporoparietal junction reported as the largest cluster.
No frequency-band prediction.
Predictive processing is offered as a foundation for the NCC search while being 'not itself a theory of consciousness'; no content/state-differential prediction is stated.
No prediction indexed to report versus no-report designs.

dimension: Consciousness measure type (objective / subjective / condition assessment / none)
justification: Compatible with subjective and objective measures; no prediction indexed to measure type.
Predicts that manipulations of interoceptive prediction (body-ownership and emotion paradigms) alter feeling states and selfhood.
No prediction indexed to task type.
Prediction is indexed to modality: feeling states arise from inferred causes of interoceptive, not exteroceptive, afferents.

dimension: Sample / population type (healthy adults / patients / non-human / computer)
justification: Predicts altered body ownership and selfhood in neuropsychiatric illness, a differential prediction for patient populations.
No technique-specific prediction.

dimension: Dependent measure / analysis type (incl. connectivity, complexity, PHI, cardiac tags)
justification: Autonomic reflexes are predicted to be enslaved by descending predictions, making autonomic/cardiac measures theory-relevant dependent variables.
Prediction-error timing is compatible but no consciousness-indexed time window is stated.
A large-scale allostatic–interoceptive system is proposed as substrate, but no consciousness-specific localisation is stated.
Systematic substrate–phenomenology mappings are promised, but no frequency-band prediction is stated.
Phenomenal states integrate supramodular response systems; the content/state distinction is not drawn, although anaesthesia evidence is reviewed as support for the integration consensus.
Evidence rests on introspective ratings; no prediction for no-report designs.

dimension: Consciousness measure type (objective / subjective / condition assessment / none)
justification: Subjective effects are the predicted outcome, but nothing is stated about objective measures.
Predicts a paradigm-specific effect: sustaining incompatible skeletomotor intentions produces stronger subjective effects than compatible ones, and smooth-muscle conflict produces none.
Predicts that tasks engaging conflicting skeletal-muscle plans, but not tasks involving impenetrable conflicts (pupillary reflex), change conscious experience.
Predicts that intersensory stimulus conflicts (ventriloquism, McGurk) are consciously impenetrable whereas conflicts involving skeletomotor plans are penetrable.

dimension: Sample / population type (healthy adults / patients / non-human / computer)
justification: Predictions are stated for healthy adults; no population-specific prediction.
fMRI was used to seek correlates of sustained incompatible intentions without a technique-specific prediction.

dimension: Dependent measure / analysis type (incl. connectivity, complexity, PHI, cardiac tags)
justification: Subjective ratings and BOLD are used; no theory-specific dependent measure is stated.
No timing prediction.
Neural correlates of conscious conflict were sought with fMRI, but the theory states no a priori localisation.
No frequency-band prediction.
Consciousness serves the somatic nervous system as a frame for skeletal muscle output; the content/state distinction is not drawn.
Report versus no-report designs are not addressed.

dimension: Consciousness measure type (objective / subjective / condition assessment / none)
justification: Measure type is not addressed.
Compatible with the conflict paradigms inherited from SIT, but the synthesis states no paradigm-indexed prediction of its own.
No prediction indexed to task type.
Olfaction is adopted as the model modality instead of vision, but no differential prediction across modalities is stated.

dimension: Sample / population type (healthy adults / patients / non-human / computer)
justification: Population is not addressed.

justification: No dependent measure is predicted.
No timing prediction.
The theory claims to begin isolating neuroanatomical substrates of conscious processes while disclaiming the implementation level; no discriminating localisation is stated.
No frequency-band prediction.
UAL is a transition marker for the presence of subjective experience in a species; it does not address content versus state contrasts within an organism.
Reported awareness is used as the criterion in the masking prediction; no prediction is stated for no-report designs.

dimension: Consciousness measure type (objective / subjective / condition assessment / none)
justification: Proposes an objective behavioural learning marker in place of report-based measures for non-verbal subjects.
Prediction (d): backward masking and related protocols that switch off conscious perception will selectively switch off UAL while leaving limited associative learning intact.
Predicts which learning tasks (trace conditioning, second-order conditioning, novel compound discrimination, reversal learning) form a correlated cluster requiring experience.
UAL is defined over novel compound stimuli as opposed to elemental ones, so the prediction is indexed to stimulus complexity.

dimension: Sample / population type (healthy adults / patients / non-human / computer)
justification: Predicts a taxonomic distribution (arthropods, cephalopods, vertebrates), and failures of UAL in blindsight patients for the blind field.
Names 'neural signatures of subjective experience' as a third route of test without committing to a technique.

dimension: Dependent measure / analysis type (incl. connectivity, complexity, PHI, cardiac tags)
justification: The dependent measure is learning performance (behavioural), not a neural measure.
No timing prediction.
Predicts co-impairment of UAL elements after brain injury (e.g. hippocampal damage and trace conditioning) but does not localise the conscious substrate.
No frequency-band prediction.
Sensory consciousness is treated as a capacity of species (which vertebrates have it); content versus state contrasts within an organism are not addressed.
Report versus no-report designs are not addressed.

dimension: Consciousness measure type (objective / subjective / condition assessment / none)
justification: Proposes hierarchies of isomorphic (somatotopic) neural representations as an objective neuroanatomical marker for sensory consciousness in place of report.
No experimental paradigm is predicted.
Task type is not addressed.
Vision is proposed as the first conscious sense, a modality-indexed evolutionary claim rather than an experimental prediction.

dimension: Sample / population type (healthy adults / patients / non-human / computer)
justification: Predicts consciousness in all extant vertebrates including the lamprey and calls for studies of fish and amphibians.
No technique is predicted.

dimension: Dependent measure / analysis type (incl. connectivity, complexity, PHI, cardiac tags)
justification: The reticular formation is said to contribute to neural synchronisation, but no dependent measure is predicted.
No timing prediction.

Localises the minimum substrate to forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain with hierarchical isomorphic nuclei, the optic tectum in fish and amphibians and the dorsal pallium/cortex in mammals, reptiles and birds.
No frequency-band prediction.
